topic: Dehydration assessment and ORS (WHO plan A, B, C)

slides.title: WHO Dehydration & ORS: High-Yield PYQs
slides.subtitle: Rapid-fire exam one-liners on Plan A, B, C & ORS composition

slides.title: WHO Dehydration Assessment
slides.subtitle: 4 key clinical parameters (IMNCI)
points: Assess 4 core signs: general condition, eyes, thirst, and skin pinch
Need >=2 signs in a category to classify as Some or Severe dehydration
Skin pinch: <=2 sec (slowly) = Some; >2 sec (very slowly) = Severe
Restless + drinks eagerly = Some; Lethargic + drinks poorly = Severe
Note: Sunken eyes & skin pinch can mislead in Severe Acute Malnutrition
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Most reliable indicator of dehydration severity is % weight loss.

slides.title: WHO Low-Osmolarity ORS
slides.subtitle: Total osmolarity = 245 mOsm/L
points: Sodium 75 mEq/L + Glucose 75 mmol/L (1:1 ratio drives SGLT-1 uptake)
Potassium 20 mEq/L, Chloride 65 mEq/L, and Citrate 10 mmol/L
Total packet weight is 20.5 g dissolved in 1 L clean drinking water
Sodium chloride 2.6 g + Anhydrous glucose 13.5 g per litre
KCl 1.5 g + Trisodium citrate 2.9 g; discard unused ORS after 24 hrs
slides.highlight: Citrate corrects metabolic acidosis & prolongs shelf life vs bicarbonate.

slides.title: WHO Plan A: No Dehydration
slides.subtitle: Home-based fluid + Zinc therapy
points: Extra ORS after each stool: 50-100 mL (<2 yrs) & 100-200 mL (2-10 yrs)
Children >10 yrs: give as much ORS or home fluid as wanted orally
Oral Zinc for 14 days: 10 mg/day (<6 mo) and 20 mg/day (>=6 mo)
Continue breastfeeding & age-appropriate feeding; never starve the gut
Danger signs to return: blood in stool, fever, poor drinking, worsening
slides.highlight: Zinc reduces stool volume, episode duration, and recurrence for 2-3 months.

slides.title: WHO Plan B: Some Dehydration
slides.subtitle: Supervised ORS in health facility
points: Dose: 75 mL/kg of low-osmolarity ORS given orally over 4 hours
Wait 10 mins if child vomits, then resume slowly (1 spoon every 2-3 min)
Reassess after 4 hours: shift to Plan A, repeat Plan B, or Plan C
Keep breastfeeding during Plan B whenever the infant wants
Persistent vomiting/refusal -> consider NG tube or shift to Plan C
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Do NOT give antibiotics routinely in acute watery diarrhea.

slides.title: WHO Plan C: 100 mL/kg IV RL
slides.subtitle: Infants (<12 mo) || Older (>=12 mo)
points: First 30 mL/kg over 1 hour || First 30 mL/kg over 30 mins
Next 70 mL/kg over 5 hours || Next 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours
Total duration = 6 hours || Total duration = 3 hours
Start ORS (5 mL/kg/hr) at 3-4 hrs || Start ORS (5 mL/kg/hr) at 1-2 hrs
slides.highlight: Fluid of choice: Ringer's Lactate (RL); NEVER give 5% Dextrose alone!

slides.title: High-Yield PYQ Traps
slides.subtitle: Don't lose marks on these twists
points: If radial pulse remains weak after 30 mL/kg bolus, repeat 30 mL/kg IV RL
In SAM, avoid routine IV fluids; use ReSoMal (Na 45, K 40 mEq/L)
Cholera (severe): Plan C + single-dose azithromycin (DOC in kids)
No IV access in Plan C? Give NG ORS at 20 mL/kg/hr for 6 hrs (120 mL/kg)
slides.highlight: Low-osmolarity ORS (245 mOsm/L) cuts stool output & IV fluid need vs old ORS.

caption:
Every single NEET-PG & INI-CET paper loves asking at least ONE question from WHO Dehydration & ORS! 💧

Swipe through for rapid-fire, exam-ready one-liners:
• WHO/IMNCI 4-sign dehydration assessment
• Exact Low-Osmolarity ORS composition (245 mOsm/L & 20.5 g breakdown)
• Plan A (+ Zinc doses), Plan B (75 mL/kg over 4 hrs) & Plan C (100 mL/kg IV RL splits)
• High-yield traps: ReSoMal in SAM, NG tube dosing & repeating the 30 mL/kg bolus

Quick quiz for the comments: What is the exact sodium & potassium concentration in ReSoMal? Drop it below! 👇

Save 🔖 & share with a batchmate!

For education only; follow local protocols.
references: WHO. The Treatment of Diarrhoea: A Manual for Physicians and Other Senior Health Workers (4th rev., 2005)
WHO / Ministry of Health & Family Welfare India. Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) Guidelines
Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics, 21st Edition (Acute Gastroenteritis & Oral Rehydration Therapy)
Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) Guidelines on Management of Acute Diarrhea & Zinc Supplementation
doctor_check: Slide 2: Corrected skin pinch cut-off for Some dehydration from '<2 sec' to '<=2 sec (slowly)' to match exact WHO IMNCI wording (<=2 sec vs >2 sec).
Slide 7: Clarified the cholera point so it specifies severe cholera needs Plan C (not all cholera) and notes single-dose azithromycin as DOC in children.

Slide 7 highlight: Replaced 'does NOT reduce stool volume directly' with the clearer exam pearl that low-osmolarity ORS (245 mOsm/L) reduces stool output and unscheduled IV fluid need compared to old WHO ORS.
